title: What if I stayed?
subtitle: E se restassi?
intro: The permit expires in eight months. Priya talks about Express Entry, Doug about a bakery of Chiara's own, Mateo about going home. In the basement, with a spreadsheet and a glass of Franco's wine, Chiara lists what she would do, what she should have done, and what she would have done if she had known. This unit builds the [[third conditional]] (if I had known, I would have…), the mixed conditional, [[wish + past perfect]], [[should have / could have / would have]], and the small vocabulary of Canadian immigration.
objectives: Fare ipotesi al passato: [[if I had known, I would have stayed]], [[if we had applied earlier, we'd have the PR by now]]
Esprimere rimpianti al passato: [[I wish I had taken the job]], [[if only I'd learned French]], [[I should have called]]
Discutere decisioni: [[should have, could have, would have]], [[I'd rather have stayed]]
Usare unless, as long as, provided that, in case per condizioni e precauzioni
Parlare di immigrazione e permessi: [[Express Entry]], [[PR]], [[sponsor]], [[work permit]], [[CRS score]]
canDo: B1 · Spoken production: can talk about hypothetical past situations and regrets.
B1 · Spoken interaction: can discuss decisions and immigration options with the right vocabulary.
B1 · Reading: can read a basic IRCC letter or guide, including the key terms.
B1 · Writing: can write a letter of regret or a reflective paragraph about choices.
B1 · Listening: can follow a conversation that mixes conditionals, modals and real plans.

sections.title: Spreadsheet in the basement
sections.intro: A Thursday night in late February. Chiara's permit expires in October. She opens a Google Sheet and starts asking what she'd do, what she should have done, and what she would have done if she had known. Listen for third conditional (if I had known, I'd have…), mixed conditional (if I'd done X, I'd be Y now), wish + past perfect, and should have.

blocks.title: Priya and the Express Entry pool
blocks.setting: Thursday 6:15 p.m., 42 Lansdowne basement. Sofia has gone to a yoga class, Priya has come over with a bottle of ginger beer, and Chiara's laptop is open to a spreadsheet with three columns: STAY, GO, OPEN BAKERY. Snow is melting outside; it is the first evening you can wear only one sweater.
blocks.register: informal between friends who talk about money and futures

lines.t: Right. Express Entry. If you had applied to the pool a year ago, you'd have been in the system by now with a CRS score. We'd be waiting for an invitation. You didn't, and that's fine; let's start now.
lines.n: Allora. Express Entry. Se avessi fatto domanda al pool un anno fa, saresti stata nel sistema con un punteggio CRS. Aspetteremmo un invito. Non l'hai fatto, va bene; ricominciamo adesso.
lines.note: If you had applied, you'd have been in the system by now: third conditional (past hypothesis). We'd be waiting: mixed conditional (past hypothesis → present consequence).

lines.t: I didn't know. I thought the Working Holiday was going to be a year and then home. I wish I'd listened when Doug told me, in September, that I should've been looking at this.
lines.n: Non lo sapevo. Pensavo che il Working Holiday sarebbe stato un anno e poi casa. Vorrei aver ascoltato quando a settembre Doug mi disse che avrei dovuto occuparmene.
lines.note: I wish I'd listened: wish + past perfect (past regret). He told me I should've been looking: reported speech with should have been + -ing.

lines.t: Water under the bridge. Let's run the numbers. Your age: 27. CRS points: around 110 if you're single. English: you'd need an IELTS General, probably CLB 9, call it 128. Education: Italian laurea, call it 112, 120 with the Educational Credential Assessment. Work experience in Canada: 10 months at a bakery doesn't count much; you'd need a year of skilled work for the 40.
lines.n: Acqua passata. Facciamo i conti. Età: 27 anni. CRS circa 110 se sei single. Inglese: ti servirebbe un IELTS General, probabilmente CLB 9, diciamo 128. Istruzione: laurea italiana, diciamo 112, 120 con l'Educational Credential Assessment. Esperienza lavorativa in Canada: 10 mesi al forno non contano molto; ti servirebbe un anno di skilled work per prendere i 40.
lines.note: Water under the bridge: idiom = acqua passata. Would need: second conditional / advice. The specifics of the Express Entry CRS score as of 2026.

lines.t: If I had a skilled job tomorrow and I had the IELTS at CLB 9 and the ECA, I'd be around 480 points. Is that in the invitation range? — It's close. Last December the cutoff was 525. In 2022 it was 489. The number moves with the quotas.
lines.n: Se avessi un lavoro skilled domani e lo IELTS a CLB 9 e l'ECA, farei circa 480 punti. È nella fascia di invito? — È vicino. A dicembre scorso il taglio era 525. Nel 2022 era 489. Il numero si muove con le quote.
lines.note: If I had a skilled job tomorrow… I'd be around 480 points: second conditional (present / future unreal).

lines.t: Alternative paths. One, PNP: Provincial Nominee Program. Ontario has an Immigrant Nominee Program with employer-driven streams. If Doug supported your file as a baker, that'd be a different track. Two, if you got married to a Canadian, that's a Spousal sponsorship. Three, if you went to a graduate program, you'd get a post-grad work permit after. There's always a path.
lines.n: Percorsi alternativi. Uno, PNP: Programma Nominati Provinciali. L'Ontario ha un Immigrant Nominee Program con flussi guidati dal datore di lavoro. Se Doug supportasse la tua pratica da fornaia, sarebbe un altro percorso. Due, se ti sposassi con un canadese, sarebbe uno sponsorship coniugale. Tre, se andassi a un programma post-laurea, prenderesti un permesso di lavoro post-studi dopo. C'è sempre un percorso.
lines.note: If Doug supported, that'd be: second conditional. If you got married, that's: zero / first conditional for a general rule. If you went to a graduate program, you'd get: second conditional.

lines.t: I wouldn't get married for a passport. — I wasn't suggesting it. I was giving you the full list. — I know. I'm tired. If I had chosen differently a year ago — if I had come here on a student visa — I would be a year into a program now, with a path. I came as a tourist with a work permit, and now the clock's running.
lines.n: Non mi sposerei per un passaporto. — Non te lo stavo suggerendo. Ti stavo dando la lista completa. — Lo so. Sono stanca. Se avessi scelto diversamente un anno fa — se fossi venuta con un visto da studente — adesso sarei un anno dentro un programma, con un percorso. Sono venuta da turista con un permesso di lavoro, e adesso il tempo scorre.
lines.note: If I had chosen differently a year ago, I'd be a year into a program now: mixed conditional (past hypothesis → present consequence). The hinge sentence of the unit.

lines.t: You still have options. Three months to study for the IELTS, apply to Express Entry, meanwhile ask Doug about a letter of support, and look at the PNP. Also, I'd be lying if I said this wasn't a lot. — I know. — If I had done the Express Entry myself when I came, I'd be already PR. I started at 420 and now I'm 490. It took three years.
lines.n: Hai ancora opzioni. Tre mesi per studiare lo IELTS, fare domanda a Express Entry, nel frattempo chiedere a Doug una lettera di supporto, e guardare al PNP. E, non lo nascondo, è un sacco di cose. — Lo so. — Se avessi fatto io Express Entry quando sono arrivata, sarei già PR. Sono partita da 420 e adesso sono a 490. Ci sono voluti tre anni.
lines.note: If I had done the Express Entry myself when I came, I'd be already PR: mixed conditional (past hypothesis → present consequence). Priya's lesson.

notes.phrase: if you had applied, you'd have been in the system · if you had chosen differently, you'd be a year in · if I had done Express Entry, I'd be PR · if Doug supported you, that'd be a different track
notes.note: Four mixed- and third-conditional sentences in one conversation. The structure of a decision looked back at and ahead.

notes.phrase: Express Entry · CRS score · PR · PNP · work permit · spousal sponsorship · post-grad work permit · IELTS CLB 9 · ECA
notes.note: The vocabulary of a Canadian permit path, 2026. These acronyms you learn once and never forget.

blocks.title: Doug and the bakery
blocks.setting: Friday 5:40 a.m., Doug's bakery, before dawn. Doug has arrived early; Chiara is prepping dough. The street outside is empty, snow lightly falling. Doug has made coffee for both.
blocks.register: informal, between a boss and a trusted employee who is becoming a friend

lines.t: Priya told me about last night. She didn't say much, just that you'd been crunching numbers. If I had been smarter in September, I would've told you about Express Entry then. I know you've only been here six months, but there's something I was going to raise after Easter. I'll raise it now, I guess.
lines.n: Priya mi ha detto di ieri sera. Non ha detto molto, solo che stavate macinando numeri. Se fossi stato più sveglio a settembre, ti avrei parlato di Express Entry allora. So che sei qui solo da sei mesi, ma c'è una cosa di cui volevo parlare dopo Pasqua. Te lo dico adesso, direi.
lines.note: If I had been smarter in September, I would've told you about Express Entry then: third conditional (past hypothesis → past consequence). I was going to raise after Easter: past intention.

lines.t: Here's the thing. I'm 72. I'm not going to be here forever. My daughter in Vancouver has her own life. If someone like you took over this bakery when I retire — three years from now — I'd be relieved. If you got a provincial nomination through the baking stream, I'd write the strongest employer letter of my life.
lines.n: Il punto è questo. Ho 72 anni. Non sarò qui per sempre. Mia figlia a Vancouver ha la sua vita. Se qualcuno come te prendesse in mano la panetteria quando mi ritirerò — fra tre anni — sarei sollevato. Se ottenessi una nomination provinciale attraverso il flusso dei fornai, scriverei la lettera di datore di lavoro più forte della mia vita.
lines.note: If someone like you took over this bakery when I retire, I'd be relieved: second conditional. If you got a nomination, I'd write: second conditional. Doug's offer is a direct second conditional.

lines.t: Doug. I don't know what to say. I came here to make bread. I didn't come to take over your bakery. — You came to live, Chiara. The bakery was a job. Life changes. Think about it. I wouldn't say it if I hadn't been thinking about it since Christmas. Priya suggested it last year. She was right.
lines.n: Doug. Non so cosa dire. Sono venuta qui per fare il pane. Non sono venuta per prendere la tua panetteria. — Sei venuta per vivere, Chiara. La panetteria era un lavoro. La vita cambia. Pensaci. Non lo direi se non ci avessi pensato da Natale. Priya l'aveva proposto l'anno scorso. Aveva ragione.
lines.note: I wouldn't say it if I hadn't been thinking about it since Christmas: second conditional (present) + if + past perfect = mixed conditional variant.

lines.t: What if I didn't want to stay for three years? What if I wanted to go back? — Then you'd go back and we'd be sad for you and happy for you. The offer isn't a trap. Here's a cheque for 1,000 dollars. It's a scholarship from the bakery for the IELTS. Pass or fail. Take it to the Thomson place next week.
lines.n: E se non volessi restare per tre anni? E se volessi tornare? — Allora torneresti e saremmo tristi per te e contenti per te. L'offerta non è una trappola. Ecco un assegno di 1.000 dollari. È una borsa di studio della panetteria per lo IELTS. Promossa o bocciata. Portalo da Thomson la prossima settimana.
lines.note: What if I didn't want to stay for three years?: a what-if question with past simple for a hypothetical. Then you'd go back and we'd be sad for you: second conditional in the response.

notes.phrase: if I had been smarter in September, I'd have told you · if someone like you took over · if you got a nomination · what if I didn't want to stay · I wouldn't say it if I hadn't been thinking
notes.note: Second and third conditionals, with one mixed. The structure of an offer that preserves the other person's choice.

notes.phrase: take over · bakery · retire · scholarship · PNP (baking stream) · employer letter · IELTS · Thomson test centre
notes.note: The vocabulary of a career-and-permit crossover.

blocks.title: Mateo and the paths you don't take
blocks.setting: Saturday 10 p.m., same week. Mateo and Chiara on the subway home from a basketball game at Scotiabank Arena. The train empties as it heads west. They're the only two with Spanish and Italian between them.
blocks.register: intimate between friends who are both making decisions

lines.t: I'm going home. In June. My mother's not well, my brother's business needs help, and I've been here two years. If I'd known at the start that I'd miss my mother this much, I would have done this differently. I would have taken a sabbatical, not a permanent move.
lines.n: Torno a casa. A giugno. Mia madre non sta bene, l'impresa di mio fratello ha bisogno di aiuto, e sono qui da due anni. Se avessi saputo all'inizio che mi sarebbe mancata così tanto mia madre, avrei fatto diversamente. Avrei preso un'aspettativa, non un trasferimento definitivo.
lines.note: If I'd known at the start that I'd miss my mother this much, I would have done this differently: third conditional. I would have taken a sabbatical: should have done, with would have.

lines.t: I'm not sure yet. If I stayed, I'd open something eventually. If I went back, I'd probably open the pasticciotto bakery in Roccamarina. Either way, pasticciotti. The question is which city. — You could do both? Six months, six months. — If I had a Canadian passport, maybe. I don't.
lines.n: Non sono ancora sicura. Se restassi, aprirei qualcosa prima o poi. Se tornassi, aprirei probabilmente la pasticceria del pasticciotto a Roccamarina. In ogni caso, pasticciotti. La domanda è quale città. — Potresti fare entrambe? Sei mesi, sei mesi. — Se avessi il passaporto canadese, forse. Non ce l'ho.
lines.note: Three second conditionals. If I had a Canadian passport, maybe: second conditional with implied apodosis (I could do both).

lines.t: If I were your Dora, I'd say: finish the year, then decide. Don't decide at eleven at night in a basement. — My Dora would say exactly that. — The train is going to be here in three stops; I'll walk you home.
lines.n: Se fossi la tua Dora, direi: finisci l'anno, poi decidi. Non decidere alle undici di sera in un seminterrato. — La mia Dora direbbe esattamente questo. — Il treno sarà qui fra tre fermate; ti accompagno a casa.

notes.phrase: if I'd known, I would have done it differently · I would have taken a sabbatical · if I had a Canadian passport, I could do both
notes.note: Third conditional + would have + base; mixed conditional (if + past simple + could + base, past condition / present ability).

notes.phrase: sabbatical · permanent move · dual-based life · passport · six months here / six there · back home
notes.note: The emigration vocabulary of a 20-something's second year abroad.

questions.q: «If I had known, I would have taken a sabbatical» — the hypothesis is:
options: In the past (impossible — the person did not know): third conditional.
questions.why: Third conditional: past condition and past consequence that did not happen.

questions.q: «If you had applied, you'd have been in the system by now» is a mixed conditional: past hypothesis, present consequence.
questions.why: The 'by now' makes it a present consequence; the past perfect in the if-clause makes the condition past.

questions.q: If I ___ (know) a year ago, I ___ (apply) to Express Entry. (3rd conditional) If I ___ (be) you now, I ___ (study, cond.) for the IELTS. (2nd conditional)
questions.n: Se avessi saputo un anno fa, avrei fatto domanda a Express Entry. Se fossi te adesso, studierei per lo IELTS.

sections.title: Decisions, immigration, savings
sections.intro: Four themes: decisions and the future, Canadian immigration vocabulary, money and savings, and a small business in Canada.

ex.t: I need to decide by June.
ex.n: Devo decidere entro giugno.

items.note: Decide + to + inf, or + that + clause, or + on + noun (decide on a path).

ex.t: This is my choice to make.
ex.n: Questa è una scelta mia.

items.note: Make a choice, have a choice (vs no choice). Different from choose (verb).

ex.t: There are three options: stay, go, or open a bakery.
ex.n: Ci sono tre opzioni: restare, tornare, o aprire una pasticceria.

items.note: Also: have the option to + inf.

ex.t: No regrets. I regret not learning French.
ex.n: Nessun rimpianto. Rimpiango di non aver imparato il francese.

items.note: Regret + -ing (regret saying) OR regret + to + inf (I regret to inform you — a formal register).

ex.t: The immigration path has four steps.
ex.n: Il percorso d'immigrazione ha quattro tappe.

items.note: Life path, career path, immigration path.

ex.t: What's your plan after June? I'm planning to apply.
ex.n: Qual è il tuo piano dopo giugno? Ho intenzione di fare domanda.

items.note: A plan vs plans. Plan to + inf, plan on + -ing (plan on applying).

ex.t: Doug asked me to take over the bakery when he retires.
ex.n: Doug mi ha chiesto di prendere la panetteria quando si ritira.

items.note: Take over (a business, a project). Also: a hostile takeover.

ex.t: She's not sure she wants to settle down in Toronto.
ex.n: Non è sicura di volersi sistemare a Toronto.

items.note: Settle down = establish a stable life in a place. Settle in = get used to a new place.

items.t: take a risk / play it safe

ex.t: I'm going to play it safe and finish the year.
ex.n: Andrò sul sicuro e finirò l'anno.

items.note: Opposite behaviours. Take a chance = take a risk.

ex.t: Every option has a trade-off.
ex.n: Ogni opzione ha un compromesso.

items.note: Trade-off between X and Y. Not the same as a compromise (a middle agreement).

ex.t: The past is water under the bridge; let's move forward.
ex.n: Il passato è acqua passata; andiamo avanti.

items.note: A classic idiom for a past regret that no longer matters.

ex.t: PR gives you most of the rights of a citizen, except voting.
ex.n: La PR dà quasi tutti i diritti di un cittadino, tranne il voto.

items.note: Status under the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act.

ex.t: You can apply for citizenship after 3 years of PR.
ex.n: Puoi fare domanda di cittadinanza dopo 3 anni di PR.

items.note: The last step. Includes the citizenship test.

ex.t: Chiara's work permit expires in October.
ex.n: Il permesso di lavoro di Chiara scade a ottobre.

items.note: Open work permit (any job) vs closed / employer-specific.

ex.t: Express Entry is the federal fast-track system for skilled workers.
ex.n: Express Entry è il sistema federale veloce per lavoratori qualificati.

items.note: Three streams: Federal Skilled Worker, Canadian Experience Class, Federal Skilled Trades.

ex.t: The CRS score determines invitations.
ex.n: Il punteggio CRS determina gli inviti.

items.note: Comprehensive Ranking System. Max 1,200; typical cutoff 480–530.

ex.t: Ontario's PNP has streams for employers and students.
ex.n: Il PNP dell'Ontario ha flussi per datori di lavoro e studenti.

items.note: Each province has its own; adds 600 points to the CRS.

ex.t: A Canadian spouse can sponsor you.
ex.n: Un coniuge canadese può sponsorizzarti.

items.note: Spousal sponsorship: a specific permanent-residence path for spouses and common-law partners.

ex.t: IRCC: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada.
ex.n: IRCC: Immigrazione, Rifugiati e Cittadinanza del Canada.

items.note: The federal department. Everything flows through its portal.

ex.t: IELTS General Training is the one for immigration.
ex.n: IELTS General Training è quello per l'immigrazione.

items.note: Max band 9. CLB 9 ≈ IELTS 7.0+. CELPIP is the Canadian alternative.

items.n: valutazione dei titoli di studio stranieri

ex.t: The ECA validates your Italian degree in Canada.
ex.n: L'ECA convalida la laurea italiana in Canada.

items.note: Educational Credential Assessment, done by WES, ICAS or similar.

ex.t: Chiara's savings are around 4,000 dollars.
ex.n: I risparmi di Chiara sono circa 4.000 dollari.

items.note: Normally plural. Savings account: conto di risparmio.

ex.t: My monthly budget: 2,500 after taxes.
ex.n: Il mio budget mensile: 2.500 al netto.

items.note: To budget (verb) = pianificare le spese. On a budget: a basso costo.

ex.t: A commercial mortgage for a bakery is different.
ex.n: Un mutuo commerciale per una pasticceria è diverso.

items.note: In North America, mortgage is both the residential and the commercial loan.

ex.t: You need at least a 20% down payment for a mortgage.
ex.n: Serve almeno un 20% di acconto per un mutuo.

items.note: North American term; in Italy = caparra / acconto.

ex.t: Doug has a small-business loan from his bank.
ex.n: Doug ha un prestito per piccole imprese dalla sua banca.

items.note: Also: student loan, car loan, personal loan.

ex.t: A good credit score in Canada: 700+.
ex.n: Un buon credit score in Canada: 700+.

items.note: From Equifax or TransUnion. Pay bills and credit-card balances on time to build it.

ex.t: RRSP: Registered Retirement Savings Plan.
ex.n: RRSP: Piano Registrato di Risparmio Pensionistico.

items.note: Tax-deductible retirement savings; taxed on withdrawal.

ex.t: TFSA: Tax-Free Savings Account.
ex.n: TFSA: Conto di Risparmio Esentasse.

items.note: Contributions are not deductible, but earnings and withdrawals are tax-free.

ex.t: Toronto's cost of living: among the highest in Canada.
ex.n: Il costo della vita a Toronto: fra i più alti del Canada.

items.note: Different cities, different pay. Vancouver and Toronto are high; Winnipeg and Montréal, lower.

ex.t: Average Toronto salary for a baker: 40–55k.
ex.n: Stipendio medio di un fornaio a Toronto: 40–55 mila dollari.

items.note: Annual, in Canadian dollars (CAD). Before taxes = gross. After taxes = net / take-home.

ex.t: Canada has a Small Business Deduction for taxes.
ex.n: Il Canada ha una detrazione fiscale per le piccole imprese.

items.note: Technical: under 500,000 CAD in income from active business. Big tax break.

ex.t: I'm a sole proprietor; my business and I are the same taxpayer.
ex.n: Sono una ditta individuale; l'attività e io siamo lo stesso contribuente.

items.note: Simplest form. No separate corporation. Taxed as personal income.

ex.t: Doug incorporated the bakery in 2003.
ex.n: Doug ha incorporato la panetteria nel 2003.

items.note: To create a limited corporation (Ltd. / Inc. / Corp.). Separate taxpayer, liability protection.

ex.t: HST is 13% in Ontario; GST is 5% federal.
ex.n: L'HST è 13% in Ontario; il GST 5% federale.

items.note: Harmonized Sales Tax (Ontario) = GST (federal, 5%) + PST (provincial, 8%). Required to register once sales > 30,000 CAD.

ex.t: A food business needs a licence from Toronto Public Health.
ex.n: Un'attività alimentare serve una licenza dalla Toronto Public Health.

items.note: Licence (noun, Canadian / British), license (verb, Canadian / US). From unit 18.

ex.t: Commercial insurance is a monthly cost of around 150 CAD.
ex.n: L'assicurazione commerciale è un costo mensile di circa 150 CAD.

items.note: Property, liability, business interruption. All separate from health insurance (OHIP).

ex.t: A commercial lease is longer and more complex than a residential one.
ex.n: Un contratto commerciale è più lungo e complesso di uno residenziale.

items.note: Different rules from residential (unit 17): no provincial standard form, usually 5+ years.

ex.t: Doug's staff: three permanent, two part-time.
ex.n: Il personale di Doug: tre fissi, due part-time.

items.note: Collective singular (the staff is / are, both). Hire staff, train staff.

ex.t: The bakery buys flour wholesale from a mill in Ancaster.
ex.n: La pasticceria compra la farina all'ingrosso da un mulino di Ancaster.

items.note: Wholesale (ingrosso) vs retail (dettaglio).

ex.t: If I launched a pasticciotto brand in Toronto, Franco said he'd help.
ex.n: Se lanciassi un marchio di pasticciotti a Toronto, Franco ha detto che aiuterebbe.

items.note: Launch a product, launch a business, launch a career. More formal than start.

sections.title: Third conditional, mixed, wish + past perfect
sections.intro: Three pieces: the third conditional (past hypothesis, past consequence), the mixed conditional (past condition, present consequence or the reverse), wish + past perfect for past regret, and the unless/as long as/provided/in case family.

blocks.title: Third conditional
blocks.rule: The if-sentence for an unreal past: a condition that didn't happen and a consequence that therefore didn't happen either. Form: if + past perfect (had + participle), + would have / could have / might have + past participle. If I had known, I would have called. If she had applied earlier, she would've been in the pool. Contraction 'd have = would have. Negative: wouldn't have / wouldn't've. Question: Would you have done it? Could and might work for 'might have been able to' and 'might have possibly'. The order of clauses is free; comma when the if-clause comes first. Variant: if-clause with past perfect continuous (had been + -ing) for a past durative hypothesis: if I had been studying harder, I would've passed.

blocks.caption: The third conditional
head: Pattern
Example
rows: if + past perfect, + would have + part.
If I had known, I would have called.
If she hadn't missed the deadline, she wouldn't have had to reapply.
could have / might have for ability / possibility
If I'd studied, I could have passed. · They might have won if the goalie had been awake.
If I had been studying harder, I would've passed.

items.t: If I had known a year ago, I would have applied to Express Entry. I didn't know. I didn't apply.
items.n: Se avessi saputo un anno fa, avrei fatto domanda a Express Entry. Non lo sapevo. Non ho fatto domanda.

items.t: If Doug had told me in September that I should have been looking, I'd have started then.
items.n: Se Doug mi avesse detto a settembre che avrei dovuto occuparmene, avrei iniziato allora.

items.t: Mateo: «If I'd known at the start that I'd miss my mother this much, I would have taken a sabbatical, not a permanent move.»
items.n: Mateo: «Se avessi saputo all'inizio che mi sarebbe mancata così tanto mia madre, avrei preso un'aspettativa, non un trasferimento definitivo.»

blocks.title: Italian periodo ipotetico tipo 3
blocks.text: Third conditional inglese = periodo ipotetico italiano della irrealtà passata: if + past perfect + would have + part. = se + congiuntivo trapassato + condizionale passato. [[If I had known, I would have called]] = [[se avessi saputo, avrei chiamato]]. Same shape, same meaning, mapping one-to-one.

items.wrong: If I would have known, I would have called.
items.right: If I had known, I would have called.
items.why: Never would in the if-clause. If + past perfect only.

items.wrong: If I knew, I would have called.
items.right: If I had known, I would have called. (unreal past)
items.why: Match tenses: past perfect in if; would have + part. in main. Just past = second conditional.

items.wrong: If I had known, I would call her.
items.right: If I had known, I would have called her. (purely past) OR If I had known, I would call her now. (mixed)
items.why: Pure third conditional has would have in main. Mixed with present-tense consequence stays would + base.

blocks.title: Mixed conditional
blocks.rule: A conditional where the if-clause and the main clause refer to different time frames. Two common patterns. (1) Past condition → present consequence: if + past perfect, + would + base. If I had studied harder, I would be a doctor now. If you had applied a year ago, you'd be in the system by now. (2) Present condition → past consequence: if + past simple, + would have + participle. If I were better organised, I would have finished yesterday. If she weren't so stubborn, she would have accepted help. The mixed conditional is extremely common when you look backward from the present or forward from the past. Also appears in regret with wish + past perfect and mixed with the present (I wish I had learned French — I'd be in Montréal now).

blocks.title: Mixed conditional = looking back from now
blocks.text: When the hypothesis is past but the consequence is in the present (right now), use the mixed pattern. [[If I had learned French when I was 15, I would be fluent now.]] — past condition (learning French at 15), present consequence (fluency now). The sentence is a bridge between a past that didn't happen and a now that is because of it.

blocks.title: Wish + past perfect, should have, unless / as long as
blocks.rule: Three families around regret and condition. Wish + past perfect: regret about the past (I wish I had taken the job = I didn't take the job, I regret it). If only + past perfect = stronger wish. Should have + participle: a thing not done that should have been. I should have called. You should have told me. Also could have (could — able to), would have (would — in another world), might have (might — possibly). Negative: shouldn't have + part. (shouldn't have said that). Interrogative in reports: Should I have called? Unless = if not (unless it rains = if it doesn't rain). As long as / provided that / providing (that) = on the condition that (first-conditional strengtheners). In case = because-maybe (take a jacket in case it rains: in case ≠ if; it's a precaution). All with the first conditional (present + will) in English, unlike se / purché in Italian which may take the subjunctive.

sections.title: Immigration paths, cost of living, the Canadian dream
sections.intro: A short map of how people actually become permanent residents in Canada, what Toronto costs today, and what starting a business as a newcomer looks like.

blocks.text: Canada's immigration system is points-based for the skilled worker (Express Entry), employer- or province-based for the Provincial Nominee Programs, family-based for sponsorship, education-based through the Post-Graduation Work Permit, and refugee-based for protected persons. [[Express Entry]] runs three streams: Federal Skilled Worker, Canadian Experience Class (if you've already worked in Canada), and Federal Skilled Trades. The [[CRS score]] (max 1,200) is calculated from age (max 110), education (max 150), language (max 160 for English + French), work experience (max 80), and more. Add 600 if a province nominates you, 50 for a brother or sister in Canada, up to 50 for a studying partner. [[Provincial Nominee Programs]] (every province has one) are the quietest and often fastest route; each has streams for employers, for international students who graduated locally, and for in-demand occupations. Processing times in 2026: Express Entry around 6 months once invited, Spousal around 12, PNP varies by province. The [[IRCC]] portal is where everything happens, and the fees run around 1,500–2,500 CAD per application plus the Right of Permanent Residence Fee of 575 CAD when you land. Chiara's path, as Priya outlined it, has three realistic options: build the CRS, use a PNP through Doug, or go back to school.

Toronto is one of Canada's two most expensive cities (the other is Vancouver). In 2026, a one-bedroom apartment rents for around 2,100–2,500 CAD a month; a basement unit like Chiara and Sofia's for 1,500–2,000; a condo downtown for 2,800+. Groceries for one are around 400–600 CAD a month; eating out is 20–35 CAD a casual meal, 60–120 a restaurant dinner. Public transit is 156 CAD monthly, hydro around 60–100, Internet 70, phone 50, insurance 30–150, gym 40. A full one-bedroom budget totals around 3,500–4,500. Salaries: starting bakery clerk 35,000–45,000, pastry chef 45,000–65,000, bakery owner — depends. The entry-level finance / tech jobs that bring people to Toronto start at 60,000–80,000; experienced engineers and doctors cross 150,000. Taxes take 25–35% in the middle brackets. A newcomer's first year is almost always break-even; the second starts building savings; the third starts allowing choices. Chiara is at the break-even threshold at six months, which is typical.

blocks.title: Starting a small business as a newcomer
blocks.text: To open a small business in Toronto as a PR or a work-permit holder, five steps. (1) [[Business number]] from CRA, free, 10 minutes online. (2) Business structure: [[sole proprietor]] (cheapest, no liability protection), [[partnership]] (two or more), or [[corporation]] (Ltd. / Inc. / Corp., tax benefits, liability shield, around 300–1,500 CAD to set up). (3) Licences: Toronto has over 100, from food-handling (ServSafe) to retail to home-based. For a bakery: Toronto Public Health certificate, Alcohol and Gaming if selling liquor, zoning permits from the city. (4) [[HST / GST]] number if sales exceed 30,000 CAD a year. (5) Insurance (property, liability, business interruption), typically 1,500–3,500 CAD a year. [[Doug]]'s bakery is a sole proprietorship that incorporated in 2003 when his wife joined the business formally. For a work-permit holder, starting a business is legal (unlike in some countries), but it doesn't give an immigration path on its own; the [[Start-up Visa]] exists for innovative businesses with endorsed investors, which is a different world.
The Canadian dream, seen from inside

The [[Canadian dream]] isn't quite the American one. It is: a stable job with health coverage; a mortgage on a semi-detached house in a suburb like Vaughan or Richmond Hill; two children who end up at the University of Toronto, Queen's or McGill; a cottage in Muskoka two weekends a month in July; retirement in Portugal, Florida or the Caribbean, depending on budget. The newcomer version is: PR in three to five years; citizenship at six to seven; a house with a mortgage in year ten; children with better English than yours; retirement wherever you can afford. The dream is less dramatic than the American one and more inclusive; it is also, famously, slower, and increasingly impossible for anyone under forty in Toronto and Vancouver because of housing costs. The pivot cities — Hamilton, Oshawa, Kingston, Halifax, Québec City, Winnipeg — now attract a lot of thirty-year-olds for exactly this reason. Chiara is deciding between the dream in Toronto and the dream of staying in the city she already loves — a decision that will take her the next eight months.
